summary.headline: Gravita Q4 FY26 revenue rose 13% YoY to INR 1,172.76 crore, but adjusted EBITDA grew only 4% to INR 112.91 crore; RML copper acquisition adds a new segment.
summary.overview: Gravita reported Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue of INR 1,172.76 crore (+13% YoY, +15% QoQ), adjusted EBITDA of INR 112.91 crore (+4% YoY, 9.63% margin) and PAT of INR 91.88 crore. For FY26, revenue was INR 4,265 crore (+10%), adjusted EBITDA INR 452.48 crore (+12%, 10.6% margin) and PAT INR 378.80 crore (+21%). Management attributed the weaker EBITDA to West Asia disruption cutting value-added sales to the Middle East (10-12% of sales) and higher inbound logistics costs. The company closed the Rashtriya Metal Industries (RML) copper acquisition in March 2026 and raised its FY26-FY29 capex plan to INR 1,700 crore.

financial_highlights.metric: FY26 EBITDA per ton: lead / plastic / aluminium

segments.name: Lead
segments.commentary: FY26 sales grew 7% to 48,889 MT on capacity additions; quarterly sales trended up. Sustainable EBITDA guided at INR 19-20/kg, with FY26 at INR 23,043/MT including arbitrage gains.

segments.name: Aluminium
segments.commentary: Volumes declined through FY26 and in Q4 due to inability to hedge and selective selling. Management says EBITDA was about INR 16/kg for the year against sustainable guidance of INR 14-15/kg; volume recovery awaits MCX hedging contract.

segments.name: Plastic
segments.commentary: FY26 EBITDA INR 16,043/MT; management guides INR 10-12/kg sustainable, with Q4 lifted by plastic price surge from supply disruption.

segments.name: Copper (RML, acquired 99.44%)
segments.commentary: Acquired for INR 560 crore; 31,200 MTPA integrated plant in Gujarat, 40% of revenue from exports, current utilisation about 50%, EBITDA about INR 45,000/MT. Consolidated from March 2026, so Q4 impact was minimal.

segments.name: Rubber
segments.commentary: Acquired a Romanian tyre company; first Indian rubber capacity (about 30,000 TPA target) due Q1-Q2 FY27 at Mundra. Guided EBITDA INR 7-8/kg.

segments.name: Lithium-ion
segments.commentary: 6,000 MTPA pilot black-mass facility at Mundra commissioned Jan 2026 for INR 14 crore; no meaningful revenue expected in FY27 and no lithium volume in the FY29 guidance.

guidance_outlook: Total installed capacity about 4.57 lakh MTPA, targeted to exceed 8 lakh MTPA by FY29; management expects about 500,000 tonnes of volume by FY29 at 60-65% utilisation.
Volume CAGR of 20-25% over the next three years; FY27 volume growth guided at 20-25%, slightly higher given FY26 misses.
Capex of INR 1,700 crore through FY29 (about INR 600 crore FY27, INR 700 crore FY28, INR 400 crore FY29), up from INR 1,200 crore earlier; copper about INR 700 crore.
Working capital guided at 85-90 days; blended tax rate guided at 17-18% versus about 15% in FY26.
Interest cost guided at INR 4-5 crore per quarter until copper recycling ramps up, when working-capital debt rises to a peak of INR 800-900 crore.

Copper recycling plant at Mandvi/Mundra (Phase 1 29,400 MTPA, INR 160 crore) expected in about 12 months; total copper capacity to reach about 100,000 MT in 2-3 years; copper EBITDA guided at INR 60-65/kg; RML EBITDA targeted at 9-10% margin in 2-3 years.
Management said it could not yet give Q1 FY27 guidance because of logistics and Middle East disruption.
capex_capacity: Mundra lead capacity expanded by 80,300 MTPA (INR 49 crore, internal accruals) in Feb 2026, taking total to 145,100 MTPA.
Phagi (Jaipur) lead addition of about 45,000 MT expected in Q1 FY27, pending government approvals; equipment already installed.
Rubber capacity (about 30,000 TPA target) at Mundra due Q1-Q2 FY27; lithium-ion second stage (refining) still to come.
RML capacity 31,200 MTPA, planned to double to about 60,000 MT in 3 years; copper recycling Phase 1 at 29,400 MTPA in about 12 months.
Capex: INR 372 crore in FY26; INR 1,700 crore planned through FY29, funded from internal accruals, with working-capital debt on top.
demand_pricing: Middle East represented 10-12% of sales, mostly value-added products; disruption cut sales and raw-material inflow, and raised inbound logistics costs.
Aluminium volumes fell due to lack of MCX hedging and selective sales; management says volumes will recover once hedging is live.

Management expects the formalisation of informal EPR/scrap supply to speed up through the government EPR exchange (MSTC), a CPCB audit framework, and a proposed reverse-charge mechanism/TDS on battery scrap.
Value-added products were 42% of FY26 revenue; Vision 2029 target is 50%.
Copper realisation is a product mix of copper and brass; RML's customers span electrical, electronics, coinage and ammunition.

qa_highlights.question: How does the INR 1,700 crore capex plan change lead capacity, and when does the Phagi lead addition come?
qa_highlights.answer: Lead target was raised to 800,000 MTPA from 700,000 MTPA; the increase is copper. The 45,000 MT Phagi addition is expected in Q1 FY27 pending government approvals.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Q4 absolute EBITDA fall, and what is the West Asia impact on Q1?
qa_highlights.answer: Copper contributed only a minimal amount in Q4 because it was acquired in March. The drop was from lost Middle East value-added sales and higher inbound logistics and material costs; Q1 impact is expected to persist in the short term.

qa_highlights.question: What working-capital and debt levels should be expected?
qa_highlights.answer: Working capital is 90 days in FY26 and guided at 85-90 days; copper is mostly imported. Working-capital debt is expected to peak at INR 800-900 crore once copper starts, up from net debt of about INR 118 crore.

qa_highlights.question: What are copper's margins, capacity path, and ROCE?
qa_highlights.answer: RML EBITDA is about INR 45,000/MT, rising to INR 65,000-70,000 with backward integration; management says consolidated copper ROCE should be 20%+. Copper capacity is 100,000 tonnes in FY29.

qa_highlights.question: What is the sustainable EBITDA per kg by product?
qa_highlights.answer: Lead INR 19-20/kg, copper INR 45/kg rising to INR 60-65/kg after recycling, rubber INR 7-8/kg; aluminium INR 14-15/kg and plastic INR 10-12/kg.

qa_highlights.question: Why is interest cost low despite gross borrowings of INR 736 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the company looks at net debt (about INR 100 crore) after using QIP proceeds for capex, working capital and the RML acquisition. Interest is guided at INR 4-5 crore per quarter until copper working capital rises.

risks_watch: Middle East disruption to value-added sales and inbound raw material and logistics costs continues into Q1 FY27.
Aluminium volume recovery depends on the MCX hedging contract, with timing uncertain.
Copper feedstock depends on imports from developed markets (US, Australia, Brazil) and new procurement networks that are not yet built out.
Working capital and debt increase materially (peak debt INR 800-900 crore) when copper ramps.
Pending approvals for Phagi lead capacity and the lithium-ion second-stage plant.
Promoter stake dilution through sale to institutions; management said there was no open-market sale.
summary.management_tone: Confident on long-term copper, capacity and volume targets, but cautious on near-term margins. Management repeatedly declined to quantify Q1 FY27 and flagged Middle East disruption and aluminium hedging as open issues.
key_quotes: So, overall, EBITDA margins would increase, but the working capital range would remain similar.
But overall, in the next three years, we are very confident of getting a CAGR of 20%-25% in volume terms consistently over the next three years.
So, it's not correct to say that the margins have been decreasing. The margins are still over and above the guidance that we have given.

growth.why: Management guides lead volume CAGR of 20-25% (FY27 slightly higher) and capacity to exceed 800,000 MTPA by FY29 on INR 1,700 crore capex, backed by the commissioned 80,300 MTPA Mundra expansion and Phagi's 45,000 MT addition pending approvals, but aluminium volumes are stalled pending MCX hedging and Q1 FY27 guidance was withheld.
